---
title: Search Field
description: "A specialized text input for search functionality, featuring a search icon and clear button."
---

import { Box, Example, SearchDelayExample, SearchField } from '../../../mdx-components';

A specialized text input for search functionality, featuring a search icon and clear button. Provides familiar search UX patterns with keyboard support and accessible labeling.

<Example>
  <Box width="300px">
    <SearchField autoComplete="off" />
  </Box>

  ```jsx
  <SearchField autoComplete="off" />
  ```
</Example>

## Placeholder text

<Example>
  <Box width="300px">
    <SearchField placeholder="Enter some text" />
  </Box>

  ```jsx
  <SearchField placeholder="Enter some text" />
  ```
</Example>

## With delay

<Example>
  <Box width="300px">
    <SearchDelayExample />
  </Box>

  ```jsx
  <SearchField delay={300} onSearch={(value) => console.log(value)} />
  ```
</Example>

## Component props

<PropertiesTable>
  <ResponseField name="label" type="string">Label text displayed above the field</ResponseField>
  <ResponseField name="placeholder" type="string">Placeholder text</ResponseField>
  <ResponseField name="value" type="string">Controlled value</ResponseField>
  <ResponseField name="defaultValue" type="string">Default value (uncontrolled)</ResponseField>
  <ResponseField name="delay" type="number">Debounce delay in ms before onSearch fires (default: 0)</ResponseField>
  <ResponseField name="onChange" type="(value: string) => void">Called on every change</ResponseField>
  <ResponseField name="onSearch" type="(value: string) => void">Called after delay (debounced)</ResponseField>
</PropertiesTable>

title: Spacing
description: "Spacing defines values that are used in margin, padding and gap properties."
---

import { Box, Column, DataColumn, DataTable, Example, ExampleBox, Label, Row, Text } from '../../../mdx-components';

Spacing defines values that are used in `margin`, `padding` and `gap` properties. The spacing scale uses Tailwind's native values.

<Example>
  <Column gap="6">
    <Column gap="2">
      <Label>Padding</Label>
      <Box border padding="4" borderRadius>
        <Text>Box with padding="4"</Text>
      </Box>
    </Column>
    <Column gap="2">
      <Label>Margin</Label>
      <Box border borderRadius>
        <Box padding="2" margin="4" border borderRadius>
          <Text >Box with margin="4"</Text>
        </Box>
      </Box>
    </Column>
    <Column gap="2">
      <Label>Gap</Label>
      <Row gap="4">
        <ExampleBox />
        <ExampleBox />
        <ExampleBox />
      </Row>
    </Column>
  </Column>

  ```jsx
  <Column gap="6">
    <Column gap="2">
      <Label>Padding</Label>
      <Box border padding="4" borderRadius>
        <Text>Box with padding="4"</Text>
      </Box>
    </Column>
    <Column gap="2">
      <Label>Margin</Label>
      <Box border borderRadius>
        <Box backgroundColor="primary" padding="2" margin="4">
          <Text color="inverted">Box with margin="4"</Text>
        </Box>
      </Box>
    </Column>
    <Column gap="2">
      <Label>Gap</Label>
      <Row gap="4">
        <ExampleBox />
        <ExampleBox />
        <ExampleBox />

    </Column>
  </Column>
  ```
</Example>

## Usage in layout components

Spacing values are used throughout the layout system. [Box](/docs/layout/box) and all components that extend it ([Row](/docs/layout/flexbox), [Column](/docs/layout/flexbox), [Grid](/docs/layout/grid), [Flexbox](/docs/layout/flexbox)) accept spacing props for controlling internal and external space.

- **padding** - Controls internal space within an element. Use directional variants (`paddingX`, `paddingY`, `paddingTop`, etc.) for more control.
- **margin** - Controls external space around an element. Supports negative values for overlapping layouts.
- **gap** - Controls space between child elements in flex and grid containers.

All spacing props accept responsive values for adapting layouts across breakpoints.

## Component props

<PropertiesTable>
  <ResponseField name="padding" type="Responsive<Padding>">true | Spacing</ResponseField>
  <ResponseField name="margin" type="Responsive<Margin>">Spacing | "auto" (supports negative values)</ResponseField>
  <ResponseField name="gap" type="Responsive<Gap>">true | Spacing</ResponseField>
</PropertiesTable>

---
title: Progress Circle
description: "A circular progress indicator that visually represents completion status."
---

import { Example, ProgressCircle } from '../../../mdx-components';

A circular progress indicator that visually represents completion status. Ideal for compact spaces, dashboards, or when you want a more visually distinctive progress display than a bar.

<Example>
  <ProgressCircle value={45} />

  ```jsx
  <ProgressCircle value={45} />
  ```
</Example>

## Show percentage

<Example>
  <ProgressCircle value={15} showPercentage />

  ```jsx
  <ProgressCircle value={15} showPercentage />
  ```
</Example>

## Component props

<PropertiesTable>
  <ResponseField name="value" type="number">Current progress value</ResponseField>
  <ResponseField name="minValue" type="number">Minimum value (default: 0)</ResponseField>
  <ResponseField name="maxValue" type="number">Maximum value (default: 100)</ResponseField>
  <ResponseField name="showPercentage" type="boolean">Shows percentage text in center</ResponseField>
</PropertiesTable>

# Zen

Zen is the design system and React component collection used by [Umami](https://umami.is).
It contains the design tokens, layout primitives, controls, and interface patterns used across
Umami products.

The components follow [shadcn](https://ui.shadcn.com/) conventions, use
[Base UI](https://base-ui.com/) primitives for interactive behavior, and are styled with
[Tailwind CSS](https://tailwindcss.com/) and CSS custom properties.

[Documentation](https://zen.umami.is/) ·
[Component source](./packages/react-zen/src/components)

## Contents

- Design tokens for color, typography, spacing, borders, and shadows
- Layout and typography primitives
- Form controls and interactive components
- Reusable interface patterns from Umami products

## Installation

```shell
pnpm install @umami/react-zen
```

### With Tailwind CSS

For projects using Tailwind CSS v4, add the Zen preset and include the package in the content
paths:

```ts
import zenPreset from '@umami/react-zen/tailwind-preset';

export default {
  presets: [zenPreset],
  content: [
    './src/**/*.{ts,tsx}',
    './node_modules/@umami/react-zen/dist/**/*.{js,mjs}',
  ],
};
```

Import the theme variables and component animations:

```js
import '@umami/react-zen/styles.css';
```

### Without Tailwind CSS

Import the full stylesheet:

```js
import '@umami/react-zen/styles.full.css';
```

## Usage

Wrap the application with `ZenProvider`, then import components from the package:

```jsx
import { Button, ZenProvider } from '@umami/react-zen';

export function App() {
  return (
    <ZenProvider>
      <Button variant="primary">Save</Button>
    </ZenProvider>
  );
}
```

See the [documentation](https://zen.umami.is/docs) for component APIs, design tokens, and patterns.

## Development

This repository is a pnpm and Turborepo monorepo:

- `packages/react-zen` contains the component package
- `apps/docs` contains the documentation site

Install dependencies:

```shell
pnpm install
```

Run the workspace in development:

```shell
pnpm dev
```

Build all packages and apps:

```shell
pnpm build
```

Lint the workspace:

```shell
pnpm lint
```

To run a command for one workspace:

```shell
pnpm --filter @umami/react-zen build
pnpm --filter react-zen-docs dev
```

The documentation development server runs at `http://localhost:9001`.
